name: Rotate dollars among blue-chip pooled money markets by trailing base + reward yield; collect the protocols' incentive budgets
thesis: Protocols pay fixed reward budgets to rent deposits, and attention decides who collects them. On blue-chip lending venues (DefiLlama category Lending, protocol TVL >= $1B, >= 1 year of history, all judged with data before each decision) a weekly-decided rotation into the five pools with the highest trailing-7-day base + reward yield, held four weeks, chosen on 2022-10..2024-06 (+0.76% a year over the savings rate actually paid, t 1.37), made +2.76% a year out of sample 2024-07..2026-10 (t 3.05, 95% interval +1.24% to +4.64%; both halves positive; +2.62% when every return is checked against share prices). All of it is reward: ignoring rewards gives -0.04%. But the result is not robust: 6 of the 18 pre-committed sibling variants lost 5.4-6.6% a year out of sample (family mean -0.16%) because they bought the Re7 USDC Morpho vault during its 100%-utilisation yield spike on 2025-11-10, four days before a 98% write-down; the chosen variant avoided it only by the timing of its slot turnover. Restricted (post hoc) to pooled money markets without curated vaults, every rewarded variant earned +0.8% to +1.3% a year out of sample (chosen parameters +1.06%, t 3.24): small, consistent, and below the bar for a go.
mechanism: Fixed incentive budgets (Aave's GHO savings rate, Morpho/Merkl campaigns, issuer-paid rewards such as AUSD on Morpho) are diluted by whoever deposits; a weekly reader of DefiLlama's trailing rates collects part of them. The yield is accrual, so entry a day late keeps ~92% (a week late ~57%). The tail is the opposite side of the same signal: a curated vault whose borrowers stop repaying shows a utilisation-driven yield spike just before its bad debt is realised.
legs: each Monday 00:00 UTC (rebalance every 4 weeks): from DefiLlama yields, take single-exposure dollar pools of the blue-chip rule (category Lending, protocol TVL >= $1B, a year of history) without the curated-vault platforms (Morpho vaults, Euler v2) - in the backtest Aave v3 36% of held days, Fluid 20%, Kamino 13%, Spark 11%, Venus core 9%, JustLend 9% - with TVL >= $1M, data fresh within 3 days, no matched hack in 30 days, deposit token >= $0.985
rank by trailing-7-day apyBase + apyReward; hold the top 5 in equal $200k slices (at $1M); keep a held pool while it ranks in the top 10
claim rewards weekly and sell them the next day; bridge with CCTP/Across when the chain changes
kill_criteria: forward ledger: trailing-13-week realised excess over the savings rate below 0
displayed reward APR of the five picks below 1pp for four consecutive weeks (the budgets have ended)
any held pool's share or receipt price more than 1% below the yield it claimed over a hold, or a matched hack at a held venue: exit the venue; two in a quarter: retire

no entry into a pool whose TVL fell below half of the prior week's maximum, or whose trailing-7 yield exceeds twice its trailing-30 (the run/spike guard; diagnostic only, it moved rather than removed the tail in the backtest)
sum of the picks' capacity (deposit at which the marginal yield falls to SSR + 1pp) below $2M
risks: tail: one write-down of a held slice (-98.6% of $200k in November 2025 for the variants that bought Re7 USDC) costs more than two years of the reward edge
concentration: the five best pools made 70% of the out-of-sample excess (Aave v3 sGHO alone 33%); campaigns end without notice
post hoc: the pooled-only universe was defined after seeing the Re7 event; only a forward test can price it
costs and size: +1.89% at $100k (Ethereum gas), +1.01% at $5M, +0.19% at $10M (dilution, swaps, bridges)
the in-sample period earned nothing: in 2023-24 Maker's 5-8% savings rate, itself a subsidy, beat every lending market
